Having diabetes doesn’t mean you can’t conceive. It means your fertility journey needs the right preparation. 🌻💛

Uncontrolled blood sugar levels can impact fertility in both men and women:

• Women: irregular ovulation, cycle disturbances, egg quality issues, and higher PCOS risk
• Men: reduced sperm count, poor motility, and increased sperm DNA fragmentation

What’s often missed is this: better glucose control is directly linked to better fertility outcomes for both partners.

Before trying to conceive, it helps to:
🌻 Optimise blood sugar levels and HbA1c (as advised by your doctor)
🌻 Consult both an endocrinologist and a fertility specialist
🌻 Review medications, nutrition, and lifestyle factors that affect reproductive health

Technology can play a big role too. Continuous glucose monitoring (CGM), insulin pumps, and fertility tracking tools now allow safer, more predictable conception planning.

Age, embryo quality and underlying diagnosis all influence this timeline. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai provides IVF Treatment in Mumbai, reviewing and adjusting the protocol after each cycle rather than repeating the same approach unchanged.

Endometrial thickness affects whether an IVF transfer can proceed, with the accepted minimum at 7 mm and the strongest implantation rates typically between 8 and 12 mm. Below that range, pregnancy rates fall noticeably. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai provides IVF Treatment in Mumbai with close attention to lining thickness and pattern, postponing a transfer rather than proceeding before preparation is adequate.

Male infertility contributes to nearly half of all conception difficulties, yet it often goes unevaluated for years while attention stays focused on the woman. Conditions like azoospermia where no sperm are present in semen can still be addressed through surgical sperm retrieval and ICSI. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai assesses male fertility as part of couple-focused care at an IVF centre in Mumbai with a thorough, evidence-based approach.

IVF, or In Vitro Fertilisation, involves controlled ovarian stimulation with daily hormone injections over 10 to 14 days, ultrasound-guided egg retrieval under sedation, laboratory fertilisation through conventional IVF or ICSI, embryo culture for 3 to 5 days, and transfer of the selected blastocyst into the uterine cavity. A blood test confirms implantation 10 to 14 days later. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, who provides IVF Treatment in Mumbai, adjusts the protocol to each patient's specific diagnosis and ovarian response.

IUI places prepared sperm directly into the uterus timed to ovulation — fertilisation occurs naturally inside the body. IVF retrieves eggs, fertilises them in the laboratory, and transfers an embryo. IUI success rates run 10–20% per cycle; IVF reaches 40–60%. For mild male factor, PCOS, or unexplained infertility under 35 with open tubes, IUI is a clinically sound starting point. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai offers both IUI Treatment in Mumbai and IVF Treatment in Bandra West, selecting the approach based on diagnosis, age, and semen parameters.

PCOS is the most common cause of anovulatory infertility — elevated androgens and insulin resistance disrupt the hormonal signals that trigger ovulation, resulting in irregular or absent cycles and fewer real conception opportunities each year. Letrozole has replaced clomiphene as the first-choice ovulation induction medication for PCOS. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, who provides Fertility Treatment for PCOS/PCOD in Mumbai, follows a stepwise approach starting with lifestyle modification before any medication is introduced.

IVF pregnancies carry a modestly elevated gestational diabetes rate  approximately 10–15% compared to 5–9% in spontaneous conception attributed largely to underlying conditions such as PCOS and advanced maternal age rather than the IVF procedure itself. Frozen embryo transfers using hormone replacement protocols show a slightly higher GDM association than natural-cycle transfers. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, whose practice includes an IVF hospital in Mumbai, incorporates metabolic screening into pre-cycle planning for high-risk patients.

A minimum endometrial thickness of 7–8 mm is generally required before an embryo transfer — thinner lining is associated with lower implantation rates and higher miscarriage risk. Causes include inadequate oestrogen stimulation, poor blood flow, intrauterine adhesions, and prior uterine procedures. Interventions such as oestrogen supplementation, sildenafil to improve blood flow, and hysteroscopic adhesion removal are used depending on the underlying cause. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, at an IVF hospital in Mumbai, evaluates endometrial response as a standard pre-transfer step.

Family planning and fertility treatment are frequently approached as a female responsibility, despite male factor infertility contributing to nearly 50% of all cases. Semen analysis, hormonal evaluation, and genetic testing for male partners are as clinically essential as female workup — yet they are often delayed or skipped entirely. Dr. Hrishikesh Pai, whose practice includes an IVF hospital in Delhi, follows a couple-centred model where both partners are evaluated before any fertility treatment protocol is designed.

This Men’s Health Month, let’s make space for conversations that feel easier to start.

Health discussions, especially around fertility and reproductive health, are often delayed because they feel confusing, uncomfortable, or overwhelming.

But clarity, openness, and understanding can make a meaningful difference. When people feel informed instead of intimidated, they are more likely to seek answers early and take confident steps towards their health.

At Nova IVF Fertility, we believe empathy begins with making every health conversation feel simple, transparent, and easier to navigate.

Male fertility is often overlooked until the journey to parenthood takes longer than expected.

But fertility is not only about sperm count. Sperm quality, including movement and overall health, can also play an important role in conception.
Advanced techniques like Microfluidics help select healthier moving sperm during IVF treatment, supporting a more personalised approach to fertility care.
This Men's Health Month, let's encourage earlier conversations, timely evaluations, and greater awareness around male fertility health.

Some dreams take a little longer to come true.

They begin as quiet hopes, become whispered prayers, and one day turn into the most beautiful reality.
This Father’s Day, we’re celebrating every dad who held on to hope, believed through the waiting, and never gave up on his dream of a family.

In IVF, precision matters at every stage.

From the collection of eggs and sperm to embryo transfer, accurate identification and verification play an important role throughout the treatment journey.

RFID (Radio Frequency Identification) technology adds an additional layer of electronic witnessing by assigning unique identifiers to biological samples and tracking them through key stages of the IVF process. This helps strengthen traceability and supports laboratory protocols designed to minimise the possibility of mix-ups.
At Nova IVF Fertility, RFID-based witnessing is integrated into our IVF laboratory processes as part of our commitment to maintaining high standards of safety and care.

A diagnosis of azoospermia can feel overwhelming, especially when a semen analysis shows no sperm. For many men, it may seem like the end of the road to fatherhood.

However, in some cases, sperm may still be present within the testes and can sometimes be retrieved through specialised procedures such as TESA, TESE or Micro-TESE. SSG Test for Pregnancy: Check Fallopian Tube Health Early

Many women weighing fertility investigations have heard about HSG and quietly wondered if there is a gentler alternative. There is. The SSG test, short for sonosalpingography, has become a preferred first line option at many fertility centres because it checks fallopian tube health using ultrasound rather than X-ray.

The SSG test for pregnancy planning works on a simple principle. A small amount of saline and air is introduced through a thin catheter into the uterus while a transvaginal ultrasound watches the fluid move through the fallopian tubes. If both tubes are open, the fluid passes freely. If there is a blockage, the SSG ultrasound shows it in real time, making it one of the most useful fertility diagnostic tests in modern infertility testing.

The SSG test procedure usually takes 10 to 15 minutes, with no radiation and only mild cramping. As an SSG tube test in fertility workup, it is increasingly chosen over HSG when conditions are favourable, especially for women who prefer a quicker, more comfortable form of fallopian tube assessment. 

An SSG test result is usually shared on the same day, with images and a clear explanation. If both tubes are open, next steps in pregnancy planning can move forward without delay.

At Motherhood Fertility & IVF Centre in Kharghar, a fertility consultation guides you on whether the SSG test procedure is the right choice for your situation.

Dysmenorrhea: Menstrual Cramps, Causes & Treatments

Painful periods are common, but persistent pain that disrupts daily life is not something women should learn to live with. Dysmenorrhea, the medical term for painful periods, affects most women at some point, and for some it points to underlying conditions that can quietly influence long term fertility.

There are two broad categories. Primary period pain happens without an underlying disease and usually settles with conservative care. Secondary dysmenorrhea is different: severe period cramps and pelvic pain may be linked to conditions such as endometriosis, adenomyosis, fibroids or pelvic inflammatory disease. Untreated, these can affect future reproductive health.

Common dysmenorrhea symptoms include cramps during period that begin a day or two before bleeding, dull lower back pain, nausea, fatigue and heavy flow. Tracking your cycle through a simple period calculator helps identify patterns your fertility doctor will want to know about.
When menstrual pain is severe, worsens over time, or comes with bleeding between periods, a fertility specialist consultation matters. 

At Motherhood Fertility & IVF Centre in Kharghar, fertility specialists assess dysmenorrhea symptoms alongside imaging and hormonal tests, so any underlying condition is identified before it affects menstrual health.

You do not have to push through every cycle in silence.

HSG Test for Fertility: What to Expect During the Procedure

An HSG is often the first investigation a woman undergoes when fertility evaluation begins, and it is also one of the most frequently googled. It sounds clinical, but the real question on most women's minds is far more human: will it hurt, what does it actually show, what happens afterwards.

HSG, short for hysterosalpingography, is an X-ray that checks whether the fallopian tubes are open and the uterine cavity is normally shaped. It is one of the most reliable forms of fallopian tube test in fertility assessment, often part of an HSG test for infertility workup before IUI or IVF. Many doctors recommend an HSG test before IUI, because tubal patency directly influences whether IUI is the right next step.

The HSG test procedure itself is short, usually around 15 to 20 minutes. A thin catheter is gently inserted through the cervix, and contrast dye is passed into the uterus. An X-ray then follows the dye as it flows through the tubes. The HSG test procedure causes only mild cramping for most women, like period pain. Your fertility team at Motherhood Fertility & IVF in Kharghar can guide pain management options.

A well-timed HSG, advised before pregnancy planning when there is a history of pelvic infection or unexplained infertility, gives clarity rather than just an image. The fallopian tube test results, often shared quickly, become the first concrete step on a fertility path that finally feels purposeful.

Why More Couples Are Choosing Frozen Embryo Transfer

For many couples going through IVF today, the question is no longer just "will this work?" but "when should we transfer?" Increasingly, the answer is later, with a frozen embryo, rather than immediately.

Embryo freezing has quietly become a routine part of modern fertility treatment.

Embryo cryopreservation is the process of freezing healthy embryos at very low temperatures so they can be safely stored for future use. In a typical IVF cycle, more than one embryo often develops after the egg retrieval process and fertilisation. Rather than transfer them all at once, embryologists at centres like Motherhood Fertility & IVF Centre in Kharghar, Navi Mumbai assess quality, freeze the strongest embryos through advanced embryo preservation, and plan a transfer when the womb is most receptive.

The embryo freezing process uses a technique called vitrification, which freezes embryos so quickly that ice crystals do not form. The embryo cryopreservation process can store them safely for years, giving couples real flexibility.

A frozen embryo transfer, often called the FET procedure, gives the uterus time to recover from IVF hormonal stimulation, which can improve implantation outcomes.

Many couples also choose blastocyst cryopreservation, where embryos are frozen at day 5, a stage linked to stronger pregnancy rates.

Thoughtful fertility treatment planning, supported by experienced embryologists.

Menstrual hygiene is not just about using sanitary products. It is about women’s health, dignity, awareness, and timely care.

On Menstrual Hygiene Day, let’s highlight the importance of maintaining proper period hygiene, changing menstrual products regularly, using clean washrooms, and speaking openly about menstrual health. Poor menstrual hygiene can lead to infections, discomfort, skin irritation, and reproductive health concerns.

Many girls and women still hesitate to talk about periods due to myths and stigma. But menstruation is a natural process, and symptoms like very painful periods, heavy bleeding, missed or irregular periods, bleeding between cycles, fatigue, dizziness, or severe mood changes should not be ignored.

These symptoms may sometimes be linked to concerns like PCOS, endometriosis, thyroid issues, hormonal imbalance, or ovulation-related problems, which can also impact reproductive health and fertility.

PCOS Officially Renamed PMOS in 2026 - What Women Should Know
 
Polycystic Ovary Syndrome (PCOS) has officially been renamed Polyendocrine Metabolic Ovarian Syndrome (PMOS) following a global medical consensus published in The Lancet in May 2026. The updated name reflects a better understanding of the condition as a hormonal and metabolic disorder, not just an ovarian condition. PMOS affects nearly 1 in 8 women worldwide and can impact periods, fertility, weight, insulin resistance, emotional wellbeing, and long term metabolic health.
 
Why this change matters:
• Highlights hormonal imbalance and insulin resistance more clearly
• Encourages earlier diagnosis and holistic care
• Recognizes fertility, metabolic, and emotional health together
• Supports better long term management and treatment planning
 
For women in India, this shift helps improve awareness and encourages more integrated reproductive and endocrine care.
